STATUS: AWAITING APPROVAL. These frames are drawn to the rulings rather than proposing them, but the album has not been approved. Under [DSX-S28] and [DSX-S29] a UBS gate turns on its album being approved, not on its walk closing — so UBS-6 lifts when this album is approved, and until then nothing here is an authoritative reference.

Nine consumers, one shell. Every frame below is the same three regions — holder · pool · detail — with the same chrome, the same verb slot and the same cap model. Only the adapter changes.

0 · The specification

What the shell owns, and what an adapter may supply. An adapter that needs something not in the right-hand column widens the shell for everyone or takes a declared escape hatch ([DSX-S1]) — never a bespoke screen.

The rules every frame obeys

  1. Consequence before action. The verb ends the detail column; nothing docks ([DSX-S3], single-scroll 2026-08-12).
  2. The reason leads. Whatever else scrolls, the reason a commit was refused is the first thing in the step ([DSX-S11]).
  3. Disabled, never hidden, for transactional failure — focusable, not activatable, reason stated (TSV-13, RPD-15).
  4. Caps render identically everywhere, with an after-action projection whenever an action changes one ([DSX-S19], [DSX-S20]). An uncapped pool draws a hatched bar, because "uncapped" has no denominator.
  5. No confirmation invented here. Confirmation is EPUX-06's authored raise-only predicate; the shell states a reversibility class instead ([DSX-S6], [DSX-S27]).
  6. On-map surfaces take the canvas region only, never the control band ([DSX-S16]).
  7. --row is a floor, not a height ([DSX-S22]).

1 · Convoy

The shared store. Items, capacity, key-item exemption, and the bulk operations.

2 · Loadout

The unit's own inventory and equip state — the surface BAT-10 and LDC-1 both delegate to.

3 · Skills

LDC-1's earned superset → equipped subset → cap, rendered.

4 · Techniques (styles)

The same frame as Skills, against max_styles and a per-use cost.

5 · Battalions

A cap of one over an unassigned pool.

6 · Shop

The drawn shop album expressed in family terms — [DSX-S25], a naming change with no redraw. Its eleven lifecycle states remain in shop_transaction_album.html.

7 · Forge

Subject-scoped like the shop. Stage 1 picks the item; the operation set is stage 2.

8 · On-map Trade

Two holders folded into one grouped pool, canvas region only.

9 · Provider convoy

The same surface with a context-declared verb set — and the battlefield shop is the shop adapter under the same rule.

10 · The dependent-choice layer

One pick, then a set that exists only because of it. Two kinds — counterpart (another instance, displaced or swapped) and operation (a transform applied to the pick). The set always takes the pool; the result and the commit verb always take the detail ([DSX-S5]). The gesture is RPD's ratified select-then-select, committing on the second selection ([DSX-S6]).

11 · Shared states

States the shell owns on every consumer's behalf. Each is drawn on the consumer where it bites hardest, and each behaves identically everywhere else.

12 · Findings from drawing

Three things the frames surfaced that no DSX ruling covers. They are findings, not rulings — options for the approval pass, in the manner of EW-1..10.

  1. Nothing caps the row measure at Expanded. The pool is 1240 px wide at 1920×1080, so an operation row puts +1 Might and 480 g roughly 1200 px apart, and the eye has no way to associate them. Every consumer has this; the forge shows it worst because its end slot is a price. The editor album met the same problem and answered it with a capped measure. Suggested: a max measure on the row's content, so extra width becomes margin rather than gap.
  2. The verb cap of two is a maximum, not a target. Battalions ship one verb and the slot looks correct with a single full-width button, so the shell must not reserve space for a second. Worth stating because a fixed two-slot row is the easy implementation and it would leave a permanent hole on the consumer with the simplest job.
  3. A pool scrolling past one screen is normal and is not what [DSX-S11] measured. The convoy pool is 2.37 screens at the Compact floor and Trade's grouped pool is 2.63 — those are lists, and lists scroll. The ~1.9-screen figure that ruling accepted was the detail column, where the consequence and the verb live. Recording it so the two numbers are never conflated in the build.
